tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List the Sesori scheduled tasks on this computer: id, name, project, schedule, whether it is on, its next run and its last outcome.

project_id.description: Only tasks of this project (a project id from the list).

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Show one scheduled task's full definition and state. Without task_id, shows this session's own task when this session is a scheduled run.

tools.name: list_task_runs
tools.description: List a task's newest runs (up to 20), newest first: when, the outcome, whether it ran late, and the start of each run's final reply. Read a whole run with get_task_run_transcript.

tools.name: get_task_run_transcript
tools.description: Read the transcript of one task run's session: user and assistant messages, tool names and short tool results. Returns the newest page first; pass its next_page as page to read older messages. Runs of a same-session task share one session, so their transcript covers every run in it.

page.description: The next_page value of the previous result.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Propose a new scheduled task in this session's project (or project_id) with this session's harness. The user allows or rejects it on their phone; nothing is created until they allow it. Each request is answered on its own; Sesori messages this session with the user's answer, so don't poll get_task for it.

time.description: daily, weekdays and weekly: the time of day.

schedule.description: One of {"kind":"once","at":DATE_TIME}, {"kind":"daily","time":TIME}, {"kind":"weekdays","time":TIME} (Monday to Friday), {"kind":"weekly","days":["monday",...],"time":TIME} or {"kind":"everyHours","hours":1-12,"start":DATE_TIME}. TIME is {"hour":0-23,"minute":0-59}; DATE_TIME is {"year","month","day","hour","minute"}; both are wall-clock time in time_zone.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/Bucharest.

project_id.description: A project id from list_tasks; this session's by default.

missed_run_policy.description: When the computer was off at a run's time: run once when back (the default), or wait for the next.

run_mode.description: {"kind":"newSession"} starts a session per run (the default); {"kind":"sameSession","autoCompact":true} continues one session, compacting it before each run when autoCompact is true.

model.description: provider/model, as this harness names it. Left out, the harness picks.

effort.description: The harness's effort (variant) id. Left out, the harness picks.

approval_mode.description: ask (the default) waits for the user on every permission; approveAll lets runs act without asking.

command.description: A shell command Sesori runs before each run's prompt, through a login shell in the task's project folder (a same-session task's session folder once it has one), stopped after 10 minutes. The prompt then carries the exit code, stdout and stderr; a stream over 500 words comes as its file's path and its last 20 lines.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Propose changes to a scheduled task. Leave out every field you are not changing; left-out fields keep their value. The user allows or rejects it on their phone. If the fields it changes are changed first, nothing is applied. Each request is answered on its own; Sesori messages this session with the user's answer, so don't poll get_task for it.

prompt.description: A new prompt text. Only for tasks that send text.

command_arguments.description: New arguments for a task that runs a command; the command stays.

time.description: daily, weekdays and weekly: the time of day.

model.description: provider/model, as this harness names it.

command.description: Same as create_task, but not for a task that runs a slash command.

remove_command.description: true stops the task's runs from running its command.

tools.name: pause_task
tools.description: Propose pausing a scheduled task. The user allows or rejects it on their phone. Each request is answered on its own; Sesori messages this session with the user's answer, so don't poll get_task for it.

tools.name: resume_task
tools.description: Propose resuming a paused scheduled task from its next time. The user allows or rejects it on their phone. Each request is answered on its own; Sesori messages this session with the user's answer, so don't poll get_task for it.

tools.name: run_task_now
tools.description: Propose running a scheduled task once now. The user allows or rejects it on their phone. Each request is answered on its own; Sesori messages this session with the user's answer, so don't poll get_task for it.

tools.name: send_page
tools.description: Ask the user on a page in the Sesori app, on whichever device they pick up: for decisions, choices between options, or input you need from them, especially several questions at once or anything that needs images. Also shows information that needs no answer. Returns at once; Sesori messages this session with the user's answers, or that they closed the page, so don't wait or poll for it, and don't ask the same thing in chat too. A page has sections, each with an optional heading, a Markdown body, images and questions. Question kinds: single (pick one option), multiple (pick any options) or text (free text). Sesori gives every question its own note field and ends every page with a free-text "Anything else?" field, so do not add your own catch-all question such as "Anything else?" or "Other comments". Images are absolute paths to png, jpg, gif or webp files, copied when sent. Limits: title 200 characters, 20 images (20 MiB each, 50 MiB in all), 50 questions, 12 options per question. Question ids are unique in the page and option ids in their question.

required.description: Must be answered to submit; false by default.

questions.description: No catch-all "Anything else?" question: the page already ends with one.

tools.name: schedule_wakeup
tools.description: Ask Sesori to send this session a prompt later, once or on repeat. Use it instead of a harness timer, a sleep or a polling loop: the user sees each wake-up in the Sesori app and can cancel it, and it survives a bridge restart. The prompt arrives as a message once this session's turn has ended, never inside one; a sub-agent's goes to its root session. Needs no approval unless it runs a command. A repeating wake-up repeats until you call cancel_wakeup, so never set it again yourself.

label.description: What it is for, in up to 100 characters. The user sees it.

prompt.description: The message Sesori sends this session when it fires.

when.description: {"kind":"in","minutes":1-10080} fires once that many minutes from now; {"kind":"every","minutes":1-10080} repeats at that interval, first one interval from now; {"kind":"daily","time":TIME}, {"kind":"weekdays","time":TIME} (Monday to Friday) or {"kind":"weekly","days":["monday",...],"time":TIME} repeat at that wall-clock time. TIME is "HH:MM", 24-hour, in time_zone.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/Bucharest, for daily, weekdays and weekly. This computer's zone by default.

command.description: A shell command Sesori runs right before it sends the prompt, through a login shell in this session's folder (its worktree when it has one), stopped after 10 minutes. The prompt then ends with the exit code, stdout and stderr; a stream over 500 words comes as its file's path and its last 20 lines. Needs the user's Allow, once, unless this session approves everything.

tools.name: list_wakeups
tools.description: List this session's wake-ups, soonest first: id, label, next time and how it repeats.

tools.name: cancel_wakeup
tools.description: Cancel one of this session's wake-ups, repeating ones included. Find ids with list_wakeups.

tools.name: watch_pr
tools.description: Watch a GitHub pull request from this session. Call it right after you open a PR, or when asked to watch or babysit one. Sesori polls the PR through the gh CLI once a minute and messages this session a [PR Monitor] report when CI finishes or fails, a review or comment arrives, a conflict appears, or the PR is merged or closed; act on every report. Reports arrive on their own, so end your turn instead of polling or sleeping. The result is the PR's current report. The watch survives a bridge restart and ends once the PR is merged or closed; a sub-agent's watch belongs to its root session. Before your first watch, read the how-to: the Sesori pr-monitor skill when you have it, otherwise get_guide with topic pr_monitor.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

auto_merge.description: Only when the user asked for this PR to be merged without human review: marking it ready then squash-merges it once. Where the default is off, the watch starts without it and the user is asked to allow it. Leave it out for the user's default from configure_pr_monitor, which is off unless they changed it.

tools.name: unwatch_pr
tools.description: Stop this session's watch of a PR. Other sessions watching it keep their watch.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

tools.name: pr_watch_status
tools.description: List the PRs this session watches: whether a report is buffered or held for CI, how long since the last report, poll failures and readiness, plus how many PRs this computer polls.

tools.name: get_pr_report
tools.description: Fetch a PR this session watches now and return its report: what changed since this session's last report, which it then counts as reported. Use it when you need the current state before the next report arrives; never call it in a loop.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

tools.name: get_pr_feedback
tools.description: Fetch the full text of a PR's feedback still awaiting your reply: each unanswered review thread with its id, and the PR comments and review summaries since your last reply. Reports only count comments, so read them here before acting on them.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

tools.name: reply_on_pr
tools.description: Post your reply on a PR: in a review thread when thread_id is given, otherwise as a PR comment. Sesori prefixes it with [Sesori reply] so the monitor never reports it back as new feedback. Reply to each review comment once you have fixed it or decided not to.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

thread_id.description: The review thread id from get_pr_feedback, such as PRRT_kwDO…; omit for a PR comment.

tools.name: mark_pr_ready
tools.description: Mark a PR ready: add the agent-ready label, handing it to a human reviewer. Call it once checks pass, expected reviews have arrived and every comment is answered, with nothing left for you to do. When auto-merge is on for the PR, this is the merge approval: Sesori makes one squash-merge attempt at the head it last polled.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

tools.name: unmark_pr_ready
tools.description: Withdraw a PR's ready label, for example when new work turns up after you marked it ready. A watched PR that still qualifies is labelled again after its next quiet report.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

tools.name: set_pr_auto_merge
tools.description: Turn auto-merge on or off for a PR this session watches, only when the user asks. With it on, the ready label is the merge approval: Sesori squash-merges the PR once it is marked ready. Turning it on asks the user to allow it where the default is off, and removes a ready label the PR already carries, so it is merged only after a fresh judgment.

pr.description: The PR as owner/repo#123 or its full URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123).

enabled.description: true to turn auto-merge on, false to turn it off.

tools.name: configure_pr_monitor
tools.description: Change the PR monitor's settings on this computer, only when the user asks: whether PRs watched without choosing auto_merge get auto-merge, for every repository or one, and the report timings. Timings apply to every watch from its next poll; the auto-merge default applies to watches started afterwards. Turning auto-merge on by default asks the user to allow it, and the result says whether it waits for their answer. pr_watch_status shows the current settings.

auto_merge.description: The auto-merge default: for every repository, or for repository alone when given.

repository.description: owner/repo: auto_merge or clear_repository then sets that repository's own default.

clear_repository.description: true to remove repository's own auto-merge default, so it follows every repository's.

quiet_minutes.description: 1 to 60: how long a report waits after the latest activity, so a burst arrives as one report. Default 2.

ci_wait_minutes.description: 5 to 240: how long a due report waits for running CI before it goes out anyway. Default 30.

idle_reminder_minutes.description: 5 to 240, or 0 for none: how long an open PR stays still before this session is reminded of it. Default 25.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Read the how-to for a Sesori tool group before you first use it. Its Sesori skill (sesori-pr-monitor, sesori:pr-monitor or pr-monitor) holds the same text: when that skill is loaded or listed, use it and don't call this tool. Topics: pr_monitor: Use right after you open a GitHub PR, when asked to watch or babysit a PR, and every time a [PR Monitor] message arrives.

topic.description: The tool group whose how-to to read.
